political_groups.name: The Kop
political_groups.note: Liverpool FC fans have always had a strong left-wing identity due to the cities history. This has been evident in the stands when fans in The Kop flew a pro-Jeremy Corbyn banner

political_groups.name: Headhunters
political_groups.note: The Headhunters were closely linked to Combat 18 and the National Front in the 1980s. While Chelsea has been commercialized for the most part, the Headhunters are still a right-wing organization. As recently as 2015 they were recorded in Paris chanting that they are racist and like it that way.

political_groups.name: Service Crew
political_groups.note: The Service Crew was very active in the 1970s and 1980s and was virulently far-right, going so far as selling Mein Kampf outside matches. They were heavily affiliated with the National Front. In the 1980s there was a concerted effort to push back again the far-right ideology, which is why Leeds United is listed as historically right-wing but not actively.

name: Hull City
record: 21W-10D-15L, 73 pts — EFL Championship 2025-26, won promotion play-offs

name: Bolton Wanderers
record: 19W-18D-9L, 75 pts — League One 2025-26, won promotion play-offs

name: Middlesbrough
record: 22W-14D-10L, 80 pts — Championship 2025-26, lost promotion play-off final

political_groups.name: Bushwackers/Beserkers
political_groups.note: The Bushwackers were a notorious far-right supporters group in the 1970s and 1980s. Affiliated with the National Front, they are much smaller than they were, but not defunct. The Berserkers are more prominent than the Bushwackers today, although probably not as prominent as the Bushwackers were in the 1970s and 1980s. The Berserkers, however, have been tied to substantial neo-Nazi and anti-Semitic activities.

political_groups.name: Zulu Warriors
political_groups.note: Zulu Warriors are a mixed race organization and have engaged in anti-racism marches.

political_groups.name: Green Brigade
political_groups.note: Green Brigade is prominently associated with Irish Republicanism and left-wing causes.

political_groups.name: Union Bears
political_groups.note: Union Bears are a strongly Loyalist organization focused on Northern Ireland remaining part of the United Kingdom. They tend towards the right do to this.

political_groups.name: Schickeria Munchen
political_groups.note: Classified as left-wing because it has taken a strong position celebrating a former Jewish club president whose family was murdered by the Nazis. This indicates a rejection of Nazism and therefore, neo-Nazism.

political_groups.name: Ultras Frankfurt '97
political_groups.note: Ultras Frankfurt 97 have multiple groups within. Some of these, such as Droogs 99 are decidedly anti-racism. However, there are some groups within Ultras Frankfurt 97 that have been known to give Nazi salutes.

political_groups.name: The Unity
political_groups.note: The Unity is clearly left-leaning having taken a clear anti-Nazi stance. They have also been involved in the settling of refugees in the Dortmund area.

political_groups.name: Borussenfront
political_groups.note: Borussenfront is a far-right organization that is particularly violent. They have taken a stand against anti-racism and anti-right-wing organizations, demanding that signs that are anti-racism and/or contrary to right-wing ideas be banned from the stadium.

political_groups.name: Wuhlesyndikat
political_groups.note: Wuhlesyndikat, while not hardcore leftists, and not necessarily engaging in violence, espouse a decidedly anti-capitalist ideology, particularly as it concerns capitalism in football.

political_groups.name: Infamous Youth / Sherwood Youth
political_groups.note: Infamous Youth was founded in order to push back against the right-wing ideology of already existing Werder Bremen supporter groups.

political_groups.name: Endstufe-Crew Bremen
political_groups.note: Members of Endstufe-Crew Bremen partook in a neo-Nazi gathering HoGeSa in 2014

political_groups.name: Sottocultura
political_groups.note: A photograph was taken in which supporters from Sottocultura were flying a flag with the SS Totenkampf. The leadership of Sottocultura indicated that they were unaware of this flag being flown.

political_groups.name: Ultras Gelsenkirchen / Marler Jungs
political_groups.note: Members of this organization have engaged in anti-Nazi activity, going so far as to block a demonstration from a far-right extremist party known as "Die Rechte."

political_groups.name: Harlekins Berlin '98
political_groups.note: Harlekins Berlin '98 displayed a homophobic banner at a game against Cologne, apparently mocking Cologne's sizable LGBTQ+ population.

political_groups.name: Hertha Frosche
political_groups.note: Hertha-Frosche is an historical supporter group for Hertha BSC, however, it was populated by skinheads and neo-Nazis. Because of it's extremely far-right membership, it is included.

political_groups.name: Inferno Cottbus
political_groups.note: Inferno Cottbus is a well known far-right organization. Members of the group are noted for having neo-Nazi tattoos, KKK style hoods, and have espoused anti-Semitic views.

political_groups.name: Ultras Dynamo
political_groups.note: Ultras Dynamo have a reputation for far-right activity. They are known for xenophobia and racist chants, and are even connected to leaders of the National Democratic Party of Germany.

political_groups.name: Blue Generation (Block U)
political_groups.note: Block U flew a neo-Nazi banner during a match Karlsruhr SC in 2024. They also chanted neo-Nazi slogans.

political_groups.name: Ultra Sankt Pauli
political_groups.note: Ultra Sankt Pauli is well known as a left-wing supporters group. They are well known for demonstrations against fascism.

political_groups.name: Collectif Ultras Paris (Virage Auteuil)
political_groups.note: The Collectif Ultras Paris are not particularly active, politically, however, they have shown support for Palestine in recent years, including the unfurling of a banner demanding a "Free Palestine."

political_groups.name: Red Tigers 1994
political_groups.note: Red Tiger 1994 identifies specifically as anti-racist and anti-fascist.

political_groups.name: Commandos Ultra
political_groups.note: Commandos Ultra has its history tied to left-wing skinheads, and has been known to engage in left-wing violence, even with other left-wing groups.

political_groups.name: Winners
political_groups.note: Winners is strongly antifa, and has been known to engage in serious violence against percevied far-right organizations.

political_groups.name: Bad Gones
political_groups.note: Bad Gones have a long history of neo-fascism dating back to their founding in 1987. They have regularly engaged in racist chanting, and show swastikas.

political_groups.name: Dogues Virage Est
political_groups.note: Dogues Virage Est displayed a tifo with SS images on it. They also engaged in a tribute to far-right leaders Jean-Marie Le Pen tribute, and a neo-Nazi figure among their supporters was identified by an official French National Assembly document.

political_groups.name: Roazhon Celtic Kop
political_groups.note: There has been considerable right-wing activity among supporters at Stade Rennais, including Nazi salutes (specifically the Kuhnen salute), as well as displaying of the SS Totenkopf. Some members of the supporter groups are also tied directly to right-wing organizations.

political_groups.name: Offender
political_groups.note: While disbanded in 2025, Strasbourg Offender are still active in the stands. They have a long history of racist and anti-Semitic actions and comments. They are also tied to other neo-fascist groups like Bastion Social.

political_groups.name: Brigade Sud Nice / Populaire Sud
political_groups.note: The Populaire Sud, previously known as Brigide Sud Nice, is one of the most virulently right-wing supporter groups in France. In recent years they have engaged in not only racist chants, but substantial racist and far-right violence as far away from Nice as Paris.

political_groups.name: Brigade Arverne
political_groups.note: Brigade Averne is known for right-wing behavior and violence during matches, including making threats and racist chants and comments.

political_groups.name: Kop Rouge 1993
political_groups.note: Kop Rouge 1993 has been tied to violence against anti-racist and anti-fascist fans with some even being found guilty in court. They have also been cited for racist rhetoric.

political_groups.name: Armata Ultras
political_groups.note: While disbanded in 2023, Armata Ultras identified specifically as anti-fascist.

political_groups.name: Red Star Fans
political_groups.note: Red Star is a committed anti-fascist fanbase.

political_groups.name: Green Angels
political_groups.note: Green Angels are a decidedly left-wing organization dedicated to anti-racism, anti-fascism and supporting working-class people.

political_groups.name: Brigade Loire
political_groups.note: Brigade Loire is decidedly anti-establishment and anti-system, with a political attitudes leaning towards the left.

political_groups.name: Boys San (faction)
political_groups.note: The largest ultra for Inter, Boys, has a long history of right-wing actions. Historically, the group has had connection to neo-fascists. In recent years, Inter Milan fans have been sanctioned for racist chants.

political_groups.name: Fedayn
political_groups.note: Fedayn is one of two main ultra groups (although it was disbanded in 2023 after its banner was stolen and destroyed). They identified as left-wing, communist, and anti-fascist

political_groups.name: Boys
political_groups.note: Boys is the other main ultra group for AS Roma and have been far-right and fascist from their founding in the 1970s.

political_groups.name: Drughi
political_groups.note: Drughi, as well as other supporter groups of Juventus, have been sanctioned for racist chants during matches.

political_groups.name: Curva Andrea Costa
political_groups.note: While there have been some right-wing factions within the Curva Andrea Costa, they are generally outnumbered by many left-wing ultra groups that developed in the decidedly left-wing city of Bologna.

political_groups.name: Lazio Ultras
political_groups.note: The fans in Lazio Ultras are openly and proudly pro-fascist.

political_groups.name: Hooligans Teddy Boys
political_groups.note: Hooligans Teddy Boys have been linked with pro-Nazi groups. Udinese fans have also espoused anti-semitic and neo-fascist views on many occasion.s

political_groups.name: Ultras Granata
political_groups.note: The tradionallty largest supporter group, the Ultras Granata have been associated with leftist politics, including support for Basque independence.

political_groups.name: Granata Korps
political_groups.note: In recent years, additional supporter groups, including Granata Korps have become larger. Granata Korps has substantial right-wing tendencies, although still largely out numbered.

political_groups.name: Ottavio Barbieri Ultras
political_groups.note: The Ottavio Barbiere Ultras, often, but not only through Fossa del Grifoni, are decidedly anti-fascist and left-wing. There was a supporter club for about 15 years, Brigata Speloncia, that was right-wing, however, it was a minority and has been disbanded.

political_groups.name: Gate 22
political_groups.note: Academic research identifies Gate 22 as a far-left ultra group that affiliates with other left-wing ultras groups, most notably Rapids.

political_groups.name: Vecchi Ultras
political_groups.note: Academic research identifies Vecchi Ultras as far-right, with the organization historically having violent clashes with Gate 22, the far-left ultra group supporting Venezia FC.

record: 22W-10D-6L, 76 pts — Serie B 2025-26, won promotion play-off

political_groups.name: Gradinata Nord Bolzano
political_groups.note: Italian nationalism is evident in the rejection of the name "Sudtirol," in favor of Alto Adige. The organization is also tied to the far-right political party Brothers of Italy.

political_groups.name: Curva Sud
political_groups.note: Curva Sud has a history of engaging in violence and racist chanting, often aimed at opposing players.

name: Vicenza
record: 27W-8D-3L, 89 pts — Champions Group A, Serie C 2025-26 (promoted)

name: Ascoli
record: 23W-8D-5L, 77 pts — Serie C 2025-26, won promotion play-off

political_groups.name: Settembre Bianconero
political_groups.note: The name of Settembre Bianconero is a reference to the Palestinian militant organization Black September that carried out the attacks at the Munich Olympics. They are neo-fascist and anti-Semitic

political_groups.name: Boixos Nois
political_groups.note: Boixos Nois began as a more left-leaning supporter group, however, over time it evolved into a far-right neo-Nazi organization.

political_groups.name: Ultra Sur
political_groups.note: Ultra Sur has strong historical ties to right-wing politics, including racist chants. Real Madrid is also closely tied to the Franco regime.

political_groups.name: Frente Atletico
political_groups.note: Frente Atletico is a radical far-right groups that has often been seen giving Nazi salutes.

political_groups.name: Supporters Gol Sur
political_groups.note: Supporters Gol Sur is a right-wing organization tied to Spanish ultra-nationalism.

political_groups.name: Celtarras
political_groups.note: The Centarras are largely considered a left-wing group. They were involved in pressuring ownership to avoid hiring Carlos Mourino, who has espoused right-wing beliefs, as manager.

political_groups.name: Bukaneros
political_groups.note: Bukaneros, among other fans of Rayo Vallecano, are well known for anti-fascist and anti-racist attitudes. In 2019 a game against Albacete was cancelled when the Rayo Vallecano fans began chants accusing an Albacete player of being a "Nazi."

political_groups.name: Ultras Yomus
political_groups.note: Ultras Yomus have been identified by police as a far-right organization.

political_groups.name: Peña Mujika
political_groups.note: Peña Mujika is associated with Basque independence and has some anti-fascist tendencies.

political_groups.name: Brigadas Blanquiazules
political_groups.note: Main supporter group Brigadas Blanquiazules has been identified by Spanish police as being far-right.

political_groups.name: Herri Norte
political_groups.note: Herri Nortes are strongly associated with Basque independence and identifies as anti-fascist. They have had some issues with violent behavior, particularly regarding a match against Roma.

political_groups.name: Biris Norte
political_groups.note: Biris Norte is reported in media as being leftist, anti-fascist, and anti-racist.

political_groups.name: Iraultza
political_groups.note: Named after an revolutionary Basque organization, Iraultza is tied to the violent ETA, which was a Marxist-Leninist pro-Basque independence terrorist organization that disbanded in 2018.

political_groups.name: Ultras Levante
political_groups.note: While not remarkably right-wing, some reports have Ultra Levante drawing support from some far-right parts of society.

political_groups.name: Indar Gorri
political_groups.note: Indar Gorri translates to "Red Force" and is virulently anti-fascist. It is also strongly pro-Basque independence, wearing the colors of the Basque flag in the stands. Additionally, the group is strongly associated with animosity towards right-leaning Real Madrid.

political_groups.name: Juventudes Verdiblancas
political_groups.note: Members of the suporter group, Juventudes Verdiblancas, have faced charged under xenophobia and racism laws in Spain. The organization has also been involved in violent behaviors.

political_groups.name: Frente Bokeron
political_groups.note: Frente Bokeron are well-known for far-right and even fascist leaning politics, and a history of violence both in stadiums and outside.

political_groups.name: Brigadas Blanquiverdes
political_groups.note: Brigadas Blanquiverdes are a far-right leaning group and at least one member has been arrested trying to enter a rivals stadium with dangerous materials.

political_groups.name: Ultra Boys
political_groups.note: Ultra Boys are a neo-fascist supporter group that, according to multiple outlets, has been involved in substantial violent activity.

political_groups.name: Brigada Amarilla
political_groups.note: Brigada Amarilla came out of the the Frente Cadiz group, and is decidedly leftist and anti-fascist, going so far as to have Che Guevara on their logo.

political_groups.name: Peña Mujika
political_groups.note: Peña Mujika is associated with Basque independence and has some anti-fascist tendencies.

political_groups.name: Ultras Violetas (far-right faction)
political_groups.note: Ultras Violetas are known to authorities for being right-wing and have a violent history with the left-wing Fossa Garrafoni.

political_groups.name: Fossa Garrafoni (1996 far-left splinter faction)
political_groups.note: Fossa Garafoni has a long history of leaning towards the left and has had a violent history with the right-wing Ultras Violetas.

political_groups.name: North Side
political_groups.note: Supporters of North Side partook in a far-right wing protest against asylum seekers in the Hague. The protest became violent.

political_groups.name: F-Side
political_groups.note: Classified as right-wing because of counterprotests to anti-Israel protest. Anti-Israel/pro-Palestine protestors tends towards the left, meaning a counter protest indicates right-wing beliefs

political_groups.name: Z-side
political_groups.note: Groningen Z-Side was founded the leader of Aktiefront Nationale Socialisten, which was a prominent neo-Nazi organization in the 1980s. More recently, there have been incidents with Groningen fans giving Nazi salutes during matches.

political_groups.name: Vak S / S.C.F.
political_groups.note: BOOS and NRC report that an "investigation shows that the club facilitates hooligans involved in antisemitic and homophobic remarks and death threats." The club was fined after members of supporter groups engaged in racist chants.

political_groups.name: M.I.-Side (hooligan firm)
political_groups.note: Supporters of SC Cambuur partook in a far-right wing protest against asylum seekers in the Hague. The protest became violent.
